scenes.heading: Plotting points and graphs
scenes.sub: Turn a table of numbers into a picture
scenes.say: A table of numbers can hide a pattern. Plot it as points on a grid, and the pattern jumps out. Today you'll turn tables into graphs and spot straight lines.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A dot-to-dot puzzle: place every dot and a picture appears
scenes.science: A table of values: plot each column and a graph appears
scenes.breaks: In a puzzle you always join the dots. On a graph, only join them if in-between values make sense.
scenes.say: Think of a dot-to-dot puzzle. One dot means little, but place them all and a picture appears. A table of values is your list of dots. Each column is one point. But unlike a puzzle, you only join the dots when in-between values make sense.

scenes.heading: From table to points
points: Each column of the table is one point
Top number is x, bottom number is y
Use equal steps along each axis
scenes.say: Read a table down each column, never along a row. The top number is x and the number underneath is y. Choose a scale with equal steps on each axis, and label both axes.

scenes.heading: Plotting the table
scenes.say: Here is the table plotted. First the grid, then the points zero one, one three, two five and three seven. Each time x goes up one, y goes up two, so a ruler passes through every dot.
scenes.caption: The points (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 7). y goes up 2 for every 1 across, so they lie on a straight line.

scenes.heading: Straight or curved?
scenes.say: When x goes up in equal steps, look at how y changes. If y changes by the same amount every time, the points lie on a straight line. That's a linear relationship. If the changes are different, like one, three, five, the points curve.

scenes.heading: Join the dots?

left.title: Continuous: join
points: Draw a line through the points

scenes.say: Water can be two and a half centimetres deep, so data like time and volume are continuous: join the points. You can't buy two and a half tickets, so counts like that are discrete: leave them as separate dots.

scenes.heading: Find a missing value
scenes.question: (1, 5), (2, 8) and (3, 11) lie on a straight line. Find y when x = 5.
scenes.say: These three points lie on a straight line. Find y when x is five. Each time x goes up by one, y goes up by three. From x equals three to x equals five is two steps, so y goes up by six. Eleven plus six is seventeen.
scenes.caption: These points lie on a straight line. Find y when x = 5. Each time x goes up by 1, y goes up by 3. From x = 3 to x = 5 is 2 steps, so y goes up by 6. 11 + 6 = 17.

scenes.heading: Reading past the dots
notes: Rule the line through the dots
Go up from x = 5 to the line
scenes.say: Now read the graph. Rule the line through one five, two eight and three eleven. From five on the x-axis go up to the line, then across to the y-axis. You land on seventeen, the same answer as the pattern.
scenes.caption: Up from x = 5 to the line, then across to the y-axis: y = 17.

points: Down the column: x then y
Same jump in y means a straight line
Can I have half? Then join the dots
scenes.say: Quick recap. Read each column as a point, x then y. The same jump in y each time means a straight line. If half a unit makes sense, join the dots. And keep equal steps on your axes. Now try the practice questions!
